scenarios.summary: A loading button tells assistive technology that it is busy and carries the loading state.
A button receives the focus and keeps it.
A button with an icon shows the icon before the label.
A loading button shows a spinner before its label.
An icon that has a label is an image with that name.
A spinner that has a label is a status with that name.
A spinner that only decorates is hidden from assistive technology.
A spinner that has a label carries it as its name.
A label shows its text.
An error shows its message.
The control of a field is named by its label and described by its hint.
While its error shows, the control of a field is described by the error and is invalid.
While the error of a field shows, the field and its control are invalid.
An input is found by its label and takes the focus.
An input whose value is refused is invalid and shows the error.
A disabled input carries the disabled state.
A loading input is busy and carries the loading state.
The reveal button of a password shows and hides the value, and says which.
An input with an icon shows the icon before the text.
A select is a combobox that takes the focus and is named by its label.
The control of a select with a hint is described by it.
A select whose choice is refused is invalid and carries the invalid state.
A disabled select carries the disabled state.
A select while something is in progress is busy and carries the loading state.
A checkbox takes the focus and is turned on by the space key.
A checkbox that is neither on nor off says so to assistive technology and carries the state.
A checkbox whose choice is refused is invalid and shows the error.
A disabled checkbox carries the disabled state.
A switch takes the focus and is turned on by the space key.
A switch whose change is being saved is busy and carries the loading state.
A switch whose change is being saved stays as it is when the space key is pressed.
A disabled switch carries the disabled state.
A code input is found by its label and takes the focus.
A code can be typed or pasted into the one element.
A code input whose code is refused is invalid and shows the error.
A disabled code input carries the disabled state.
A heading is announced as a heading and shows its text.
A paragraph shows its text.
A link receives the focus and keeps it.
The link of the current place is marked for assistive technology and carries the current state.
A link that opens in a new window or tab says so to assistive technology.
A link of the variant button is still a link that goes to an address.
A link with no address is not a link: it is marked disabled and carries the disabled state.
An alert shows its message.
An alert with a title shows the title above the message.

steps.text: Your account has one way in
Add a second way to sign in.

scenarios.summary: Pressing the dismiss button hides the alert.
A card shows its header, its body and its footer.
A table shows its column header and its rows.
A table with no rows shows its message.
A table whose rows are being replaced says that it is busy and carries the loading state.
A column that cannot be sorted by shows its name and is not a link.
A column that the list can be sorted by is a link.
The column that the list is sorted by tells assistive technology the direction.
A row shows the cells that it holds.
A cell shows its text.
A data table has a search field and a choice of the page size.
A data table with no rows shows its message instead of the table.
A data table with no rows and no message of its own shows the words that the component writes itself.
A data table says that it is busy while another page loads and carries the loading state.
An open dialog is announced as a modal dialog named by its title and carries the open state.
A dialog shows its title, its body and its actions.
Pressing the close button closes the dialog.
The Escape key closes the dialog.
A dialog that is not open is not shown.
A toast shows its title and its message.
A toast that never hides itself is hidden by the dismiss button.
The region that holds the toasts announces what appears in it without interrupting the user.
A loading button is marked as disabled for activation while it keeps the focus.
A disabled button carries the disabled state.
An icon that only decorates is hidden from assistive technology.
An icon that has a label carries it as its name.
The control of an input with a hint is described by it.
A read-only input carries the read-only state.
The control of a checkbox with a hint is described by it.
A checkbox whose choice is refused carries the invalid state.
The control of a switch with a hint is described by it.
A switch whose change is refused is invalid and carries the invalid state.
The control of a code input with a hint is described by it.
A code input whose code is refused carries the invalid state.
A code input whose code is being checked says that it is busy and carries the loading state.
A pagination says how many rows there are and which page is shown, and the line is announced when it changes.
On the first page the controls to go back are not links and carry the disabled state; the controls to go on are links.
On the last page the controls to go on are not links and carry the disabled state; the controls to go back are links.
A pagination offers a choice of the page size, named by its words.
A pagination with an empty list of sizes shows the summary and the controls but no choice of the page size.
A textarea is found by its label, takes the focus and says that it takes several lines.
A textarea whose value is refused is invalid and shows the error.
The control of a textarea with a hint is described by it.
A textarea with a limit shows how many characters are used out of it.
A textarea with a limit and no text yet says the limit in words.
A disabled textarea carries the disabled state.
A read-only textarea carries the read-only state.
A loading textarea is busy and carries the loading state.
An avatar with a picture is an image that is named by the name of the person.
An avatar with no picture shows the first letters of the first and the last word of the name.
An avatar whose name is one word shows one letter.
A decorative avatar is hidden from assistive technology.
A badge shows its words, which carry the meaning.
A badge with a dot shows the dot before the text.
A badge with an icon shows the icon before the text.
A closed menu shows only its button, which says that it opens a menu; pressing it opens the list, names the list by the button and puts the focus on the first item.
The down arrow on the button opens the list and puts the focus on the first item.
The arrow keys, Home and End move the focus among the items.
Escape closes the list and the focus goes back to the button.
A heading is shown above the items and is not one of them.
A menu holds a link and an item that is a button.
The item of the place the user is in is marked as the current page.
A disabled item says so to assistive technology.
A separator is shown between two groups of items.
A file that is chosen is held by the control and shown in the list with a button that removes it.
A control for one file holds the file that was chosen last.
A control for several files keeps the files that were chosen before and adds the new ones.
The button of a file takes it out of the control and out of the list.
A file of a kind that is not allowed is not held by the control; it is listed with the reason, and the control is invalid.

steps.text: notes.txt is not a kind of file that can be used

scenarios.summary: A file larger than the limit is not held by the control; the reason names the limit in megabytes.
Files beyond the most that the control holds are refused, and the files that were held stay.
While the host sends the files the control shows how far it has come, as a bar with a name, and it is loading.
An error that the host gives marks the control as invalid and is tied to it.
A disabled control carries the disabled state and cannot take a file.
While files are dragged over the place the control carries the dragging state; when they are dropped the state goes and the control holds the files.
The words that the author gives replace the words of the component in the place that is clicked.
Without words of the author the place that is clicked says that a file can be dragged there.

steps.text: Drag a file here or click to choose

scenarios.summary: The crop area is hidden until a picture is chosen; then it is shown, tied to the line that says the keys, with the zoom at its smallest.
Without moving or scaling, the part that is kept is the middle of the picture, in the size that was asked for.
The arrow keys move the picture the way a drag in that direction would: moved to the left, the part that is kept is further to the right.
Dragging the picture to the left moves it the way the arrow key does.
At the largest scale the part that is kept is a small part of the picture: the zoom stops where the part has no fewer pixels than the file to make, and the picture can be moved to the corner.
The zoom does not go beyond the limit that the author gives.
The Enter key on the crop area keeps the part inside the frame, as the button does.
A frame of three to one gives a file of the size that was asked for, from the middle of the picture.
A picture with fewer pixels than the file asked for is kept at its own resolution, in the shape of the frame.
A picture that a camera stored on its side is cropped as it is shown, upright.
A picture with transparent parts is put on white when the file is a jpeg.
A picture with transparent parts keeps them when the file is a png.
After the crop the control says that the file was made, and the stage stays so that the user can crop again.
The button that chooses another picture shows the chooser again and takes the file that was made away.
A file that is not a picture is refused: the crop area stays hidden, nothing is made, and the control is invalid.
The crop area takes the focus, so that the keys can move the picture.
A disabled control carries the disabled state.
A picture of many megapixels is read and cropped like a small one: when the step ends the control is idle and the crop area is shown, and the part that is kept is the middle of the picture.
